images.title: How big is a square kilometre
images.purpose: Show that a square kilometre is 1000 m by 1000 m, so it holds 1000000 square metres.
images.composition: One large square with its side lengths, a tiny square in one corner for a single square metre, one equation below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, the main figure large and centred with generous empty margins on all sides, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills, nothing else in the frame. A large square drawn with a thick #2B2B2B outline and very light #0072B2 fill. Label '1000 m' under the bottom side and '1000 m' beside the left side; '1 km²' in large bold text at the centre. In the bottom left corner a tiny filled #CC79A7 square, with a thin leader line to the label '1 m²' (the tiny square is drawn larger than true scale so it can be seen). Below the figure one line: '1000 × 1000 = 1000000 m²'. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: 1 km² is 1000 m by 1000 m, which is 1000000 m², not 1000 m².
images.description: Show that a square kilometre is 1000 m by 1000 m, so it holds 1000000 square metres.
images.context: Concept T9.C3; one image showing only the main idea.

image_decisions.why: The size gap between a square metre and a square kilometre is the misconception; one picture of the big square fixes it.
